candidates.name: Acropolis Museum

candidates.name: Roman Agora
candidates.content: This area became the main marketplace of the city after the Ancient Agora to the west became primarily a religious facility under Roman rule. It houses the Tower of the Winds, an eight-sided tower with a different wind deity on ea

candidates.name: Kerameikos
candidates.content: The site of the ancient cemetery of Athens. It also houses the Dipylon Gate, where the Panathenaic procession would begin. Its museum showcasing many of the grave stele and other archaeological items found on the grounds. The site

candidates.name: The Lyceum
candidates.content: An ancient temple here hosted lectures by Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle, and early meetings of the Athenian Assembly. Aristotle made the temple the home of his school, the Lyceum. It hosted the world's first zoo and botanical gar

candidates.name: National Archaeological Museum of Athens
candidates.content: This is the largest and most popular of Athens' many museums, and is usually very crowded. Its vast collection includes treasures unearthed from Mycenae by Heinrich Schliemann; a staggering array of sculpture including the earlies

candidates.name: Benaki Museum of Greek Culture
candidates.price: €9, students, seniors, people with disabilities and teachers €7; temporary exhibitions €7/€5; €25 Benaki Museum Experience ticket entitles the visitor to one entrance per exhibition in all the Benaki Museum buildings, valid for 3 months
candidates.content: Visit the beautiful Neoclassical main building which houses collections of Greek art, from ancient times through the Byzantine period and the modern state. Open late and for free on Thursday evenings. The museum shop is a good pla

candidates.name: Museum of Cycladic Art
candidates.hours: Mon Wed-Sun 10:00 to 17:00, open till 20:00 on Thu
candidates.content: Holds the second largest collection of Cypriot antiquities in the world outside Cyprus, after the Metropolitan Museum in New York. Some of the most popular exhibits include the Cycladic figurines, the idols from Early Bronze Age C

candidates.name: Museum of Greek Folk Art
candidates.price: €2; students from non–EU countries, senior citizens from EU €1; under 19, students from EU (with ID), and people with disabilities free
candidates.content: An excellent museum of its type. Too often neglected by visitors to Athens, even though it is in the heavily touristed Plaka neighbourhood. Displays include artefacts, tools, primitive painting, folk pottery and interior decor. It

candidates.name: Vorres Museum
candidates.hours: Sat Sun 10:00-14:00, weekdays by appointment only and for groups of at least 20 people
candidates.content: A museum of folk and contemporary art. Its grounds cover 320,000 m2 (80 acres) including several buildings, gardens and courtyards. Its collection includes over 6,000 pieces covering 4,000 years of Greek history and art. The museu

candidates.name: National Historical Museum
candidates.content: In the old parliament building, this museum contains a large collection of historic documents such as the first constitution of Greece, furniture, equipment from the revolution. If you are lucky you may see the old session room.

candidates.name: National War Museum
candidates.content: The National War Museum is the only significant surviving public project of the military dictatorship which ruled Greece 1967 - 1974. The museum's displays are old fashioned and biased towards the more successful periods of Greek

candidates.name: Parthenon
candidates.content: This massive temple was built in the 5th century BC in thanksgiving for the Greek victory over Persian invaders. It was later converted into a Christian church, then an Ottoman mosque. It was mostly intact until 1687, when a Venet

candidates.name: Stoa of Attalus
candidates.content: This building was reconstructed in the 1950s from its original foundations, incorporating as much of the original structure and materials as possible, with limestone quarried from Piraeus and roof tiles made of clay from Attica. I

candidates.name: Kaisariani Monastery and Gardens
candidates.content: A nice escape from the city in the foothills of Mount Hymettus. Walking trails. There's a functional monastery one can walk in, and several ruined chapels or basilicas up on the walks.

candidates.name: Kanellopoulos Museum
candidates.content: A small but excellent museum displays artifacts from Mycenean Greece on, and includes some wonderful Persian artifacts.

candidates.name: National Gallery
candidates.content: It's one of Greece's main art institutions and features paintings and works of art from some of Greece's and Europe's best from the 19th and 20th centuries. Emphasis is given to popular Greek contemporary artists including Giannis

candidates.name: Museum of Ancient Greek Technology Kotsanas
candidates.content: A very interesting museum that should not be missed. Excellent demonstration of some fantastic inventions of the ancient Greeks. Most models are functional and can be interacted with. Some can only be interacted with when a docent

candidates.name: Numismatic Museum
candidates.content: The building of the museum is one of the most beautiful in Athens, and was built by Ernst Ziller and was used as the residence in Athens of Schliemann. The collection contains thousands of ancient coins and ancient Greek, Roman, B

candidates.name: Spathario Museum
candidates.content: The first and unique museum of shadow theatre in the world, dedicated to the famous Greek shadow theatre character "Karagiozis".

candidates.name: Pnyx
candidates.alt: Ancient Greek: Πνύξ; Greek: Πνύκα, Pnyka
candidates.content: If Athens is the birthplace of democracy, then Pnyx is its cradle. Around 507 BCE this rocky hill, overlooking the Akropolis, became the meeting place for the ekklesia, Athens' early democratic assembly. This site thus witnessed a

candidates.name: Ancient Agora
candidates.price: €20, reduced €10, ticket valid for both the archaeological site and the museum
candidates.content: The site of the ancient city centre is a green space with a beautiful view of the Acropolis. It was built as a multipurpose area, then evolved into a religious area over time. The Ancient Agora was eventually abandoned and then la

candidates.name: Church of the Holy Apostles
candidates.content: From the 11th century, one of the oldest churches in Athens.

candidates.name: Arch of Hadrian
candidates.content: A monumental gateway resembling a Roman triumphal arch. It was built around 131 AD to honor the Roman emperor Hadrian, an admirer of Greek culture, for his many benefactions to the city.

candidates.name: Panathinaiko Stadium
candidates.content: The stadium that housed the first modern day Olympic Games of 1896. Earlier versions of the stadium date as far back as 330 BCE. It's an enormous, white, marble stadium, with a horseshoe configuration.

candidates.name: Athens Municipal Art Gallery
candidates.content: Paintings of Greek painters of the first half of the 20th century are displayed.

candidates.name: Museum of Greek Popular Musical Instruments
candidates.content: Includes exhibits of traditional Greek musical instruments, with recordings of most of them.

candidates.name: Hellenic Air Force Museum
candidates.content: A number of old planes from as far back as the 1930s can be seen here.

candidates.name: City of Athens Technopolis
candidates.content: An industrial museum of incomparable architecture. The centre has assisted in the upgrading of a historic Athens district.

candidates.name: Stavros Niarchos Cultural Centre
candidates.hours: 06:00-20:00 (gardens open till 22:00 in summer; National Library open 06:00-00:00)
candidates.content: This complex in the seaside suburb of Kallithea has stunning views from its terrace all the way to the Acropolis on one side and of the coast on the other. Evening concerts and other cultural events take place here. The building,

candidates.name: Athens Festival
candidates.content: Runs from May to October each year. Offers a wide spectrum of events covering almost every taste. Outside Athens, try to attend a performance at the ancient theater of Epidaurus – a truly unforgettable experience.

candidates.name: Athens Concert Hall
candidates.content: This venue attracts world-famous artists all year round.

candidates.name: National Gardens
candidates.content: A Peaceful and beautiful park in the centre of Athens, easily the coolest place to hide from the summer sun. Wander around, check out the quirky art that seems to sprout up every now and again, look on in disbelief at the "zoo", s

candidates.name: Dionysiou Aeropagitou Street
candidates.content: This landmark street starts from the Temple of Olympian Zeus at Vasilissis Olgas Avenue, continues under the southern slopes of the Acropolis near Plaka, and finishes just beyond the Temple of Hephaestus in Thiseio. The street has

candidates.name: Parnitha National Park
candidates.content: Well-marked paths, gorges, springs, torrents and caves do the protected area. Hiking and mountain-biking in all four mountains remain popular outdoor activities for many residents of the city.

candidates.name: Pedion tou Areos
candidates.content: Covers 27.7 hectares, near the National Archaeological Museum.

candidates.name: Balux
candidates.content: One of the best bars in Athens for the specific style, to call it a bar is an understatement. Balux is large complex set right on the water in Glyfada, one of the trendiest areas of the city. It is open during the summer for swimm

candidates.name: Metamatic_taf
candidates.content: Independent space organising and hosting cultural events related to all forms of artistic production, and a point of social gathering. Great cocktails and a variety of jazz/soul music.

candidates.name: Rebetiki Istoria
candidates.content: One of the best rebetica clubs, often open in summer when most others are closed.

candidates.name: Showroom
candidates.content: Nice cafe/restaurant.

candidates.name: Ydria
candidates.content: This sprawling cafe-restaurant that takes up a large part of Platía Paliás Agorás along Adhrianoú St. at the western end of Plaka, is a good place for daytime coffee or a before or after dinner drink. They also serve food, though

candidates.name: Costa
candidates.content: Standard stuff, but has a nice air conditioned and quiet upstairs seating area overlooking the square.

candidates.name: Playce
candidates.content: A really nice cafe where you can play board games whilst drinking your coffee. Very popular.

candidates.name: Filion Cafe
candidates.content: Start the day with a double shot of dark espresso at this cafe in the Kolonaki neighbourhood, just north of Syntagma Square.

candidates.name: Vegan Beat Athens
candidates.content: Vegan street food restaurant. Tasty food and nice people that work there. A good place for all vegans and even non-vegans. The true Parthenon of the vegan scene of Athens. Excellent vegan souvlaki.

candidates.name: The Traditional
candidates.content: Traditional Greek food. If you want to eat in a quality village tavern in the center of Athens, you will come here. Great roasted food, salads and appetizers! The food is handmade.

candidates.name: Krasopoulio tou Kokkora
candidates.content: Among the best traditional Greek restaurants in Athens downtown. The owner is smiling, polite and very keen to assist. A wonderful casual lunch or dinner spot. Fresh ingredients and substantial portions.

candidates.name: Aspro Alogo
candidates.content: An excellent little Greek restaurant well worth finding. Everything is fresh and delicious and the service is great. The owner is a helpful and generous guy. Attentive and familiar treatment.

candidates.name: Atlantikos
candidates.content: Nice little place with great seafood selection. The meals look simple and are delicious. The portions are quite large and the quality price ratio is very well balanced. One should go in time and expect quite some waiting time to g

candidates.name: Karavitis
candidates.content: a severely traditional taverna where the speciality is stamnaki, or beef, potatoes and cheese cooked in tomato sauce in an individual clay pot. The fried zucchini here are also always good. Mostly patronized by Greeks, but there i

candidates.name: Zeus Xenios
candidates.alt: pronounced and sometimes spelled Zefs in modern Greek
candidates.content: literally in the shadow of the Acropolis, offers quieter and less expensive dining than the many touristy tavernas lining Mnesikleous whose touts will try to snare you as you walk up the hill. The view isn't as spectacular as you

candidates.name: Cafe Avissinia
candidates.content: A remarkable restaurant, serving refined and creative innovations on traditional Greek dishes in a chic setting. It is on the square of the same name which is the venue of the main Athens flea market. This is an interesting place

candidates.name: Kafeneio Ivis
candidates.content: Very authentic Greek tavern, frequented by locals. Great value for money. Warm welcome, nice terrace and fast service.

candidates.name: Lefka
candidates.content: A long-established traditional taverna with spacious outdoor seating. Closed Sundays.

candidates.name: Το Κιούπι (To Kioupi)
candidates.content: Known among some expatriates as "the hole in the ground," this is a basement taverna serving authentic, inexpensive traditional Greek fare.

candidates.name: Pame Psirri
candidates.content: On Agii Anargiri square -- Psiri. A "mezedopolio" where local singers sing rempetika music.

candidates.name: Laiki
candidates.content: A fruit, vegetable and fish market. Good fun.
